goal: Establish a fresh-context reviewer mechanism and a deterministic review protocol, so an implementation can be judged against its sealed contract by a reviewer that never saw the implementer's reasoning.
non_goals: Any hook — PreToolUse, PostToolUse, or otherwise
Runtime enforcement of allowed_paths, forbidden_paths or tool permissions on a live agent
Automatic task routing, automatic role selection, or automatic dispatch of a review
Automatic merge, or making any GitHub check or reviewer required
Changing .claude/settings.json permissions, production credentials, or anything in Supabase
Judging this repository's existing code — the deliverable is the mechanism, not a review
acceptance_criteria: A reviewer subagent is defined whose context does not inherit the implementer's conversation, and whose read-only posture with respect to the implementation is enforced by the platform rather than by instruction alone
The reviewer's brief is generated deterministically from the sealed contract and the base/head refs, with no free-text field an implementer can use to editorialise
The protocol has a closed verdict vocabulary, and a verdict outside it is rejected
Every acceptance criterion of the contract under review must be addressed individually; a result that leaves one unaddressed cannot approve
An approval must carry an explicit statement that no merge-blocking findings remain — an empty findings list alone never approves
Every finding carries a severity, evidence, and the violated contract criterion or invariant where one applies
Any tool or protocol failure resolves to BLOCKED, never to approval

Deterministic fixtures prove the protocol catches a diff outside allowed_paths, a touched forbidden path, unmet acceptance criteria, risk under-classification, production-effect under-classification, a reviewer attempt to modify the implementation or contract, a missing or unreadable contract, and a review-tool failure — and that a clean fixture can approve
stop_conditions: The available subagent mechanism cannot establish fresh context — report rather than simulating independence with another prompt in the same context
Making the reviewer read-only would require a hook or runtime enforcement, which is out of scope
The work turns out not to fit workflow-authority / r3 / none — report before implementing
notes: Governance step for Workflow Hardening 2, sealed before implementation. .agent/tasks/** is absent from allowed_paths and is on the always-forbidden floor, so the implementing task cannot edit or re-seal this contract. Classification: workflow-authority because the reviewer is control-plane machinery (task-contract infrastructure and validators); r3 because it is CI/workflow authority; production_effect none because it neither reaches production nor deploys learner-facing code on merge.
